content: Nifedipine is prescribed for the treatment of vasospastic angina, which is a type of chest pain caused by spasms in the coronary arteries. This diagnosis is confirmed if the patient meets any of the following criteria: (1) the patient experiences angina at rest, accompanied by an elevation in the ST segment on an electrocardiogram (ECG); (2) angina or coronary artery spasms are induced by the administration of ergonovine; or (3) coronary artery spasms are observed during angiography. Even if a patient has significant fixed obstructive coronary artery disease, they can still be diagnosed with vasospastic angina as long as the above criteria are met. Additionally, nifedipine may be considered in cases where vasospasm is suspected but not definitively confirmed. For example, this includes patients whose chest pain has a variable threshold during physical exertion, those with unstable angina showing ECG findings consistent with intermittent vasospasm, or those whose angina does not respond adequately to nitrates or beta-blockers. Nifedipine is also indicated for the management of chronic stable angina, also known as effort-associated angina, in patients who do not show evidence of vasospasm. It is particularly useful for patients who continue to experience symptoms despite receiving adequate doses of beta-blockers or organic nitrates, or for those who cannot tolerate these medications. Clinical trials lasting up to eight weeks have demonstrated that nifedipine can reduce the frequency of angina episodes and improve exercise tolerance in patients with chronic stable angina. However, the long-term safety and sustained effectiveness of nifedipine in this patient population have not been fully established. Limited studies suggest that combining nifedipine with beta-blockers may provide additional benefits for patients with chronic stable angina. However, the effects of this combination therapy, particularly in patients with impaired left ventricular function or abnormalities in cardiac conduction, are not well understood. For the treatment of hypertension, nifedipine extended-release tablets are indicated. They can be used as a standalone therapy or in combination with other antihypertensive medications.
